fields.quests[].id: Stable id = source filename without .txt (e.g. S0000001, QLBD01, 00B00Y00, _BRISIEN).
fields.quests[].filename: Source file name with .txt inside the pack or questline quests directory.
fields.quests[].source: dfu-quest-pack (265 pinned DFU quests) or online-questline (39 port questline scripts).
fields.quests[].playerFacing: false for the 21 __DEMO scripting examples, which are not player-facing quests and should be excluded from the guide.
fields.quests[].displayName: DisplayName header; null for 28 trigger/demo scripts that declare none.
fields.quests[].group: { raw: quest-list group or family, label: humanised, source: where the group came from }.
fields.quests[].listed: true when a QuestList-Classic/DFU row names the file (offered by guilds/social groups).
fields.quests[].questList: Raw list row: membership, minReq, flag, notes, disabled, listSource. minReq < 10 = guild rank/player level, >= 10 = reputation.
fields.quests[].startsBy / questee / questor /: Values from the file header comments (null when the file does not state them); questId falls back to the Quest: line.
fields.quests[].notes: Every other file header comment (design/audit notes, not dialogue).
fields.quests[].messageCount / messageIds: How many QRC panels exist and the sorted, de-duplicated numeric message ids. No panel text, keys or variant sentences are published.
fields.quests[].journalMessage: The { key, id } of the journal/QRC panel a journal line came from; its text is not published.
fields.quests[].taskNames: QBN task identifiers (the scripted objective steps); action lines stay in the local full extraction.
fields.quests[].timeLimit: The started timer: { clock, start, end, minDays, maxDays, raw }. Clock arrays and variable names stay in the local full extraction.
fields.quests[].resources: QBN resource names only (items, persons, places, foes); kinds/raw declaration lines stay in the local full extraction.
fields.quests[].reward: Declared QBN item resources: gold flag, item names, named items, summary; sheet-backed quests add sheetPay pay bands and sheetNamed item names.
fields.quests[].objectiveSource: Where a page generator can find the objective: sheet (ids only here), journal (id only) or tasks.
fields.quests[].sheet: Public sheet reference: objective/outcome ids, pay bands, success id, named item names, branch ids; text lives in the local full extraction.
fields.questlines[]: 14 online lines: { id, group, tier, title, opens, steps:[{quest,title,step,needs}], stepCount } (port-authored display strings, no DFU dialogue).
fields.counts: Totals, per-group counts and parse/coverage figures; gaps lists unresolved or missing inputs.

gaps.declaredMessageHeaderNote: The source Messages: header counts compiled QRC records; parsed panels can differ. Informational, not a parse failure.

QL12 (2026-10-19; bible/06-Systems/Questlines-Arc.md section 4.1): THE BURNING DOORS, step 1 of 5.
The port's own script on DFU's machine (systems/questlines/qlLines.js). Started by the line's runner, never offered
by a questor: the letter is the offer. Lore: Ysolde Marnhel wrote "On the Burning Doors" (systems/breachBook.js).
AUDIT QUESTLINES LINES-24: the purse is the line's tier-3 band (300 to 600), as every other step of the Cycle's; and
the letter signs off with her name (LINES-26: DFU's pack names a quest letter by its last line, ItemHelper.cs:335).

reward.summary: gold reward declared; sheet pay: standard, none

notes: QL12 (2026-10-19; bible/06-Systems/Questlines-Arc.md section 4.1): THE BURNING DOORS, step 2 of 5.
The port's own script on DFU's machine (systems/questlines/qlLines.js). Started by the line's runner, never offered
by a questor: Ysolde's letter is the offer. A coven of Dagon's Faithful in a remote dungeon, as a Mages Guild quest
sends one (M0B30Y04's `reveal` and `place foe`): find it, slay its Summoner, take the rite-book the Summoner carries
(`give item` to a foe before it is placed, as B0B81Y02's map). The branch is the player's, asked when the book is in
hand: read it, or carry it to Ysolde shut (the Mages Guild's standing, on the sheet). Lore: the faithful's rite is the
port's own, as "On the Burning Doors" tells it (systems/portBooks.js).

reward.summary: gold reward declared; sheet pay: greater, standard, none

notes: QL12 (2026-10-19; bible/06-Systems/Questlines-Arc.md section 4.1): THE BURNING DOORS, step 3 of 5.
The port's own script on DFU's machine (systems/questlines/qlLines.js). Started by the line's runner: Ysolde's words
are in the journal at once (the last step ended at her table). WITNESSED (net/questlineClaims.js, `rite`): the step
waits on the act its receipt is - the faithful's rite broken at a Dagon's Breach (`ql act rite-broken 1`, said by
net/gate/gateClaims.js). Then her letter, and a meeting where she pays. Two clocks, as DFU's guild quests keep one: a
generous one for the act (the player may need weeks to reach a breach), a second for the meeting once it is done.

reward.summary: gold reward declared; sheet pay: standard, none

notes: QL12 (2026-10-19; bible/06-Systems/Questlines-Arc.md section 4.1): THE BURNING DOORS, step 4 of 5.
The port's own script on DFU's machine (systems/questlines/qlLines.js). Started by the line's runner: Ysolde's words
are in the journal at once, and she waits at her hall. WITNESSED (net/questlineClaims.js, `breach`): the step waits on
a Dagon's Breach closed (`ql act breach-closed 1`, said by net/gate/gateClaims.js - a kill, never the rite alone).
A visit before the door is shut is answered and cleared, as DFU's guild quests clear an early click (M0B30Y04's
`_clearclick_`). Lore: the Warden's will holds the door ("On the Burning Doors", systems/portBooks.js).

reward.summary: gold reward declared; sheet pay: standard, none

notes: QL12 (2026-10-19; bible/06-Systems/Questlines-Arc.md section 4.1): THE BURNING DOORS, step 5 of 5 - the line's end.
The port's own script on DFU's machine (systems/questlines/qlLines.js). Started by the line's runner: Ysolde's letter,
then her table. She tells why Dagon's Faithful cage the Sigil Broker, and asks where the embers the player carried out
of the breaches should go - one `ask`, three choices, the line's outcome (the sheet's `guild`, `order`, `broker`).
Lore: canon - Dagon gave the Dark Seducers their wings; the Covenant of Akatosh and Alessia, kept by the Dragonfires;
the Order of the Hour is Akatosh's. The port's own - the Broker, a Seducer who sells Dagon's sigils for embers to
the ones who close his doors, and the cage his faithful keep her in (bible/11-Multiplayer/World-Bosses.md, "The
caged Broker"). AUDIT QUESTLINES LINES-23: the Covenant is Akatosh's with the Emperors' blood (portBooks.js "The
Covenant") - the Order of the Hour is Akatosh's, never the Covenant's keeper (1032, 1041).

reward.summary: gold reward declared; sheet pay: standard, greater, none; named: Ysolde's Ember-Rod, Seal of the Hour, Broker's Dusk-Wing Mantle

notes: QL12 (2026-10-19; bible/06-Systems/Questlines-Arc.md section 4.1): THE COVENS' HOARD, step 1 of 3.
The port's own script on DFU's machine (systems/questlines/qlLines.js). Started by the line's runner, never offered
by a questor: Ysolde's letter is the offer, as the Burning Doors' first was (QLBD01). The act: three of the covens'
gold-lit champions slain in the Elite Dungeons (`ql act elite-foe-slain 3`, said by scenes/dungeonContext.js). Then
her table, where she pays; a visit before the third falls is answered and cleared, as DFU's guild quests clear an
early click (M0B30Y04's `_clearclick_`). Lore: canon - the Spire's portal keys, surrendered by the Imperial
Secretary in 3E 398. The port's own - the covens hoard them in the deep places (bible/11-Multiplayer/Elite-Gates.md).

reward.summary: gold reward declared; sheet pay: standard, none

notes: QL12 (2026-10-19; bible/06-Systems/Questlines-Arc.md section 4.1): THE COVENS' HOARD, step 2 of 3.
The port's own script on DFU's machine (systems/questlines/qlLines.js). Started by the line's runner: Ysolde's words
are in the journal at once. A coven lieutenant in a remote dungeon, as a Mages Guild quest sends one (M0B30Y04's
`reveal` and `place foe`), named by the machine's own name banks (`=lieutenant_`, Foe.cs SetFoeName); the key is
given to the foe before it is placed (B0B81Y02's map) and brought back to Ysolde (`toting`, as DFU's deliveries). The
key is a quest item that only LOOKS like a Weir Key in its coven-cloth (a talisman, its words in message 1017): the
real one is the account service's to pay, at the line's last step (net/questlineClaims.js `key`).

reward.summary: gold reward declared; sheet pay: standard, none

notes: QL12 (2026-10-19; bible/06-Systems/Questlines-Arc.md section 4.1): THE COVENS' HOARD, step 3 of 3 - the line's end.
The port's own script on DFU's machine (systems/questlines/qlLines.js). Started by the line's runner: Ysolde's letter,
then her table, and one `ask`: keep the Weir Key, or give it to the Order of the Hour to be sealed. The outcome ids are
the service's words (net/questlineClaims.js `key`: the choice `keep` is paid a real Weir Key, once an account). Both
paths pay the Guild's fee in gold; the seal path a rung up besides (the sheet's `greater`). AUDIT QUESTLINES LINES-4:
the keep path paid nothing of its own (`ql paid`) and said "Ysolde slides the key across the table to you" - but the
key is the ACCOUNT's, once (server-account/src/questlines.js: only while `ql_key` is 0), so a second character of the
house who kept it was paid nothing at all and told the key was theirs. Now the fee is paid either way, and 1030 says
before the choice, and 1040 after it, that a house has the key once (the port's family is the account's characters -
tutorialCatalogue.js `legacy`).
Lore: canon - the Spire's portal keys and the Weir Gate; the Empire sealed the Spire. The port's own - the torn halls
the key's road reaches now (bible/11-Multiplayer/Elite-Gates.md section 3).

reward.summary: gold reward declared; sheet pay: standard, greater, none; named: Hourkeeper's Linen Signet

notes: STAR8 (2026-10-20; bible/11-Multiplayer/Starfall.md section 7): THE THIRTEENTH OF FROSTFALL, step 1 of 4.
The port's own script on DFU's machine (systems/questlines/qlLines.js). Started by the line's runner while the
Starfall runs (`needs: ['starfall']`), never offered by a questor: the letter is the offer. A Wyrd Sister at a tavern's
door hands it over - the Witches' Festival's vendors are Glenmoril's own (`ql act wyrd-met 1`, said as her window
opens: scenes/witchesHost.js) - and if the player holds a fallen star before meeting one, Morwen saw its thread burn
and her raven brings a note instead (AUDIT STAR8 T1: not a courier's clock - online REST8 cuts a delay to the short
wait, two real minutes of play, and a raven on a clock would beat every Sister). One or the other, never both.
Witnessed (net/questlineClaims.js `star`, the j1 receipt): it waits on a fallen star held (`ql act star-held 1`),
then on the player at the Glenmoril Coven (`permanent GlenmorilCoven`, the lycanthropy cure's own place - $CUREWER).
A coven is an open-air place in Daggerfall - one block of the wilds (WITCAA00.RMB), no building and no dungeon, so no
quest marker to stand a person on - and DFU's own quests meet one as this does, by the player's arrival (`pc at`,
S0000007's). Morwen meets the player at its fire. Lore: canon - the Witches' Festival on the 13th of Frostfall
(TEXT.RSC 8392), the music in the woods (Q0C4XY04.QRC: "The witches must be celebrating"), the Glenmoril Witches who
summon Hircine alone (FACTION.TXT 419, `summon: 4`), Mephala's summoning day the Festival's own
(systems/daedraSummoning.js). The port's own: the covens' rite that sings a star down and binds it in black thread,
Morwen of Glenmoril, her sisters at the taverns' doors, her raven.

notes: STAR8 (2026-10-20; bible/11-Multiplayer/Starfall.md section 7): THE THIRTEENTH OF FROSTFALL, step 2 of 4.
Begun by the raven's letter (the line's runner starts it an hour after the first). The Sisters of the Bluff spin the
black thread at their coven nearest the capital (`permanent BluffCoven`, the region of Daggerfall). A coven is an
open-air place with no quest marker (WITCAA04.RMB - QLTF01 says why), so its people come out of the dark when the
player arrives, as DFU's own ambushes do (`create foe ... 1 times`, started by the arrival, so a return while the
coven stands brings no second): the Spinner and three of her sisters, each named and stood as a woman (`ql name ...
female`, systems/questlines/qlActions.js QlName - Foe.cs SetFoeName rolls a man as often as not). AUDIT STAR8 S1: the
spindle is the player's as the Spinner falls (`get item`, never on her body - a body the cull, a teleport or a load
takes would take it too), and a coven gone unfought (`ql gone`: the Spinner unkilled and none of them standing - the
encounters' 120 m cull, a death's teleport) is called up again at the next arrival; her death costs the Sisters of
the Bluff's favour (`change repute with`, a stand-in of their faction - A0C0XY04's `_dummymage_` way). Then Morwen at
the Glenmoril Coven's fire, met once on the player's arrival with the spindle, and her question: a length unwound to
sell (`unwound`, and Morwen buys it herself rather than see it sold) or the spindle given whole (`wound`); with the
spindle in hand her patience has no end (`stop timer`). Lore: canon - the Sisters of the Bluff (FACTION.TXT 423), the
Coven on the Bluff (MAPS.BSA, the quest table's BluffCoven). The port's own: the Spinner, her spindle, the starlight
spun on it.
